4. Even after PR #3780, there are known edge cases (PR #3915, May 2026) where it must fall back to plain `z.union()`.

The source quote says "union" -- the claim inflates this to "discriminated-union-style," which is a technically meaningful distinction in Zod. A plain union of response shapes (200, 400, 500) does not provide discriminated union behavior because there is no common discriminator property across HTTP response shapes of different status codes.

What TypeScript static analysis, type-level safety, and compile-time protection mechanisms should an OpenAPI SDK wrapper use? "Hey API generates a single Zod schema per endpoint response, and when the endpoint describes multiple responses, the generated schema is a union of all possible response shapes, enabling discriminated-union-style runtime validation from OpenAPI specs."

5. Is this a marketing claim / press release / cherry-picked benchmark / forum speculation?
